CausalChain: Overexpression of circMAT2B -> Upregulation and maintenance of oncogenic PKM2 (nuclear dimer) -> Enhanced aerobic glycolysis and lactate production -> Acidic tumor microenvironment stabilizes HIF-1α -> Promotion of angiogenesis, metastasis and sorafenib resistance -> Inhibition of circMAT2B -> Shift from PKM2-dominance to PKM1-like activity, favoring oxidative phosphorylation -> Reduced lactate, destabilized HIF-1α -> Decreased angiogenesis and improved drug response
Hypothesis: Inhibition of circMAT2B in HCC cells will shift the metabolic balance from aerobic glycolysis towards oxidative phosphorylation by reducing oncogenic PKM2 activity, thereby decreasing lactate-mediated HIF-1α stabilization, suppressing angiogenesis and metastasis, and enhancing the sensitivity of HCC to sorafenib therapy.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by enhanced aerobic glycolysis and associated metabolic reprogramming that facilitates proliferation, metastasis, and drug resistance, notably to sorafenib. Emerging evidence suggests that noncoding RNAs, including circular RNAs like circMAT2B, significantly influence the expression and isoform equilibrium of key glycolytic enzymes such as pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2). Here, we propose that targeted inhibition of circMAT2B induces a metabolic switch from oncogenic PKM2 activity towards a more oxidative phosphorylation‐oriented state by favoring PKM isoform transition. This shift is hypothesized to reduce lactate production and extracellular acidification, thereby destabilizing HIF-1α signaling, suppressing angiogenesis and invasion, and ultimately increasing the chemosensitivity to sorafenib in HCC. Our hypothesis underlines a novel interplay between noncoding RNA regulation and metabolic reprogramming in HCC that may be exploited to overcome drug resistance.
